title: Is there a shorter way to arrange the same data?
description: An ordered list repeats a shoe size once for every student who wears it. The video turns the same nine sizes into a frequency table, and Keeko asks where else the two ways of arranging data can be used in class.
teaching_notes: One idea: an ordered list keeps every entry, while a frequency table writes each value once with its count. Watch for children who forget to check that the counts add up to the number of students.

source: Two ways to arrange: an ordered list and a frequency table
video_script.why: The child sees that the same data can be arranged in more than one way, each with its use.
video_script.substitution: the first row of the book's shoe-size data, nine students
video_script.anchor: Jia's ordered list of shoe sizes
video_script.payoff_line: Size three has frequency two, size four has frequency four, and size five has frequency three.

final_answer.spoken: size three has frequency two, size four has frequency four, size five has frequency three

names.Jia: teacher who records and orders the shoe sizes of her students

never_show: the whole class data of 27 sizes
answers about size 5 or larger than 4 in the class
video_script.design: The ordered list on the left; on the right, a short table where each size appears once with its count.

beats.on_screen: title card with the ordered row of nine shoe sizes: 3 3 4 4 4 4 5 5 5

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the ordered row
marks.again: the repeated sizes light up in groups
marks.ask: a question mark lights up above the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an idea from your book, where Jia arranged shoe sizes in order.
<bookmark mark='again'/>The ordered list repeats the same size again and again.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is there a shorter way to arrange the same data?

beats.on_screen: the ordered row and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the ordered row beside an empty two-column table headed Size and Number of students

marks.long: the repeated entries of the row light up
marks.once: the empty table appears beside the row

narration: <bookmark mark='long'/>A long list repeats a size once for each student who wears it.
<bookmark mark='once'/>Instead, we can write each size once and put its count beside it.
Such a table of values and their counts is a frequency table.

marks.given: the ordered list is written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the ordered list: three, three, four, four, four, four, five, five, five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the same data as a frequency table

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to arrange the same data as a frequency table.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the first column holds each size once: 3, 4, 5

marks.sizes: the three different sizes appear once each in the first column

narration: <bookmark mark='sizes'/>Step one, write each different size once in the first column.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: count the entries of each size: 3 has 2, 4 has 4, 5 has 3

marks.count: the entries of each size are counted and the count is written in the second column

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count the entries of each size and write the count beside it.
Size three has two entries, size four has four, and size five has three.

marks.check: the counts are added and match the nine students

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step three, add the counts to check the table.
Two and four and three make nine, which is the number of students.

beats.on_screen: Answer: size 3 has frequency 2, size 4 has frequency 4, size 5 has frequency 3
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Size three has frequency two, size four has frequency four, and size five has frequency three.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a classroom board with the headings colour, toy and school subject, and a row of children giving answers

marks.ask: the three headings appear on the board
marks.use: the answers of the children are arranged as an ordered list and as a table

narration: <bookmark mark='ask'/>Keeko asks where we can use these two ways in class.
The book suggests asking classmates for a favourite colour, toy or subject.
<bookmark mark='use'/>Each set of answers can be arranged as an ordered list or as a frequency table.
